summary: Wooden fire tower on Silver Mountain, Ottawa NF; sources date it variously from the 1920s to 1940; long gone, with concrete pedestals still visible at the summit.

facts.design: Wooden fire tower, 40 ft (1971 notice); a 14 by 14 ft live-in lookout is also described
facts.status_note: Hiking guide says the tower is long gone; concrete pedestals remain near the summit. No source gives a removal date.

access.note: On Ottawa National Forest land; the guide says the public is allowed and encouraged to visit. No tower remains to climb.

visit.trail_note: 0.9 miles from the parking area to the summit, intermediate difficulty

events.note: L'Anse Sentinel: Ejnar Uddenberg to take charge of the Silver Mountain fire tower (April 1930).
Uddenberg named as towerman at the Silver Mountain fire tower.
Uddenberg named with the Silver Mountain fire tower in an August 1934 notice.
Date given by the 1971 notice. Disputed: a 1930 newspaper item already shows a tower in use.
Trail and stairway up to the lookout tower under construction.
Vandals shot out four windows and broke into the tower.
Bids for the tower's removal sent out by the Ottawa National Forest (September 1971).

evidence.supports: Silver Mountain is a massive basalt outcrop
evidence.quote: Silver Mountain is a massive outcrop of basalt that rises over 250’ above the surrounding landscape.
Silver Mountain is 36 miles south of Houghton, a journey that will take about an hour by car.

evidence.supports: Wooden fire tower on the summit from the 1920s to the early 1970s
evidence.quote: From the 1920s through the early 1970s, a 40’ high wooden fire lookout tower was located on top of Silver Mountain.

evidence.supports: Tower long gone; concrete pedestals still visible near the summit
evidence.quote: Though it’s long gone now, the concrete pedestals the tower once stood upon are still visible near the summit.

evidence.supports: Summit is in the Ottawa National Forest; public allowed and encouraged to visit
evidence.quote: Silver Mountain is conveniently located in the Ottawa National Forest which means the public is not only allowed to visit, but actively encouraged to!

evidence.supports: Hike of 0.9 miles from the parking area to the top
evidence.quote: It’s only 0.9 miles from the parking area to the top
Getting to the top of Silver Mountain requires an intermediate-difficulty hike over rugged terrain.

evidence.supports: 1971 notice in The Wakefield News: wooden tower erected in 1940, 40 feet high
evidence.quote: is a wooden structure which was erected in 1940. It is 40 feet high

evidence.supports: April 1930: Uddenberg to take charge of the Silver Mountain fire tower
evidence.quote: Ejnar Uddenberg left Wednesday for Silver Mountain, Laird Township, where he will have charge of the Silver Mountain fire tower.

evidence.supports: June 1931: Uddenberg named as towerman at the tower
evidence.quote: Ejnar Uddenberg, towerman at the Silver Mountain fire tower, was in town Thursday evening of last week.

evidence.supports: August 1934: Uddenberg named at the tower
evidence.quote: Ejnar Uddenberg of the Silver Mountain fire tower was called to Baraga Friday to assist in work at the Conservation building.

evidence.supports: November 1963: trail and stairway to the tower under construction
evidence.quote: A trail and stairway up Silver Mountain to the Silver Mountain Lookout Tower is being constructed.

evidence.supports: October 24, 1969 (Ironwood Daily Globe): vandals shot out four windows and broke into the tower; the Ontonagon District ranger says hunters cause damage every fall
evidence.quote: Vandals recently shot out four windows and broke into the fire tower at Silver Mountain on the Ontonagon Ranger District. Ontonagon District ranger Owen Gusler commented that every fall damage occurs to facilities from hunters in the forest.

evidence.supports: September 1971: Ottawa National Forest sent out bids for removal of the tower
evidence.quote: Bids for the removal of the Silver Mountain Lookout Tower have been sent out to interested parties, according to an announcement by Ottawa National Forest Supervisor Joseph H. Harn.

evidence.supports: The September 1971 notice carrying the bids and the 1940 description is credited to The Wakefield News
evidence.quote: Anyone interested in bidding on the Silver Mountain Lookout Tower should contact the Forest Supervisor, Ottawa National Forest, in Ironwood, Michigan." (The Wakefield News)

evidence.supports: Aircraft had made fire towers nearly obsolete by 1971
evidence.quote: more modern methods of fire detection employing aircraft have been used which make fire towers almost obsolete.

evidence.supports: Michigan history: the author knows of only one fire lookout used in Michigan, on Silver Mountain; live-in lookout 14 by 14 ft, held by guy wires
evidence.quote: There were also one-off towers and at least one Fire Lookout located in Michigan. I am aware of only 1 fire lookout used, which was located on the top of Silver Mountain. This live-in lookout measured 14’x14′ and was held down to the mountain by guy wires.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Brief said unknown. The 2022 hiking guide says the tower is long gone, and the 1971 removal bids make removal plausible. No source gives the year it came down.

notes_for_editor: Built date is contested: a 1920s start (guide), 1930 use (L'Anse Sentinel items quoted by the Forest Lookouts page) and 1940 erection (1971 notice). Design is also contested: 40 ft wooden tower (1971 notice) vs a 14 by 14 ft live-in lookout (Michigan fire tower history). height_m 12.2 is 40 ft converted; treat it as the 1971 figure only. Removal date not found; the guide says gone and 1971 bids for removal were sent out. The 1971 notice places the tower about 8 miles east of L'Anse, and the compiler notes that it was actually west; not used in the story. The Dirty Mule access-road page returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Brief coordinates were not checked. No photos captured.
